who: Richard F. Hamm, historian of American law and society at the University at Albany; PhD Virginia, 1987 according to his CV.

Lists a Virginia PhD in American History in 1987 and Albany faculty appointments from 1990 onward.
Public record names Richard Hamm but provides no education, employment, works, biography or researcher links.

who: Lara Putnam, historian of Latin America and the Atlantic world at Pittsburgh; PhD Michigan, 2000.

evidence.says: Lists the Michigan PhD, 2000, Latin American and Atlantic history fields, and The Company They Kept (2002).
Fernandez Montes de Oca explicitly names Lara Putnam as his advisor in the acknowledgments of his Pittsburgh dissertation.
Authority for Putnam, Lara cites The Company They Kept (2002) and supplies the variant name Lara Elizabeth Putnam.

notes: Doctorate, institution, named student and the authority-linked publication agree.

who: Stanley K. Schultz, historian of American cities at Wisconsin–Madison; studied at the University of Chicago.

evidence.says: Department obituary says Schultz studied with Daniel Boorstin at Chicago, joined Wisconsin in 1967, retired in 2005 and continued teaching another year; lists Constructing Urban Culture.
Department identifies Stanley Kenton Schultz as its professor of history.
Authority for Schultz, Stanley K. cites Constructing Urban Culture under that name.

notes: Wisconsin career, Chicago education and the distinctive book establish the match. The brief search did not independently verify the exact doctorate year.

who: Harold E. Selesky, historian of colonial America and military history at the University of Alabama; PhD Yale.

evidence.says: John Lloyd Minney’s 2016 Alabama History PhD dissertation names Harold E. Selesky as committee chair.
Lists Selesky as associate professor, with a Yale PhD, and author of War and Society in Colonial Connecticut (1990). The page gives the degree year as 1972.
Authority for Selesky, Harold E. cites War and Society in Colonial Connecticut and his Ezra Stiles guide.

notes: The named dissertation chair and matching authored works establish identity. Alabama’s page gives 1972 for the PhD whereas AHA gives 1984; retain the discrepancy.

who: Steven L. Schlossman, historian of education and juvenile justice at Carnegie Mellon; PhD Columbia, 1976.

evidence.says: Identifies the History and Public Policy professor, Columbia PhD 1976, specializing in education, childhood and juvenile justice; lists Transforming Juvenile Justice.
Reports his arrival at Carnegie Mellon in 1988 and identifies Jessie Ramey as a 2009 History PhD graduate involved in his teaching-award nomination.
Authority for Schlossman, Steven L. cites Love & the American Delinquent (1977) and Delinquency Prevention in South Chicago (1984).

notes: The compatible name, Columbia doctorate, Carnegie Mellon career spanning the student years, and specialized juvenile-justice scholarship support the match.

who: J. F. C. (John) Harrison, historian of British social and labour history at Wisconsin–Madison from 1961 to 1970, subsequently Sussex.

evidence.says: Malcolm Chase’s scholarly obituary identifies J. F. C. (John) Harrison as the labour historian who joined Wisconsin’s history department in 1961.
Repository copy documents his Wisconsin appointment, British labour-history work and later Sussex professorship.
Candidate authority resolves to John Parker Harrison, the National Archives Latin American specialist who compiled Guide to Materials on Latin America in the National Archives (1961).

notes: Reject candidate p-46111: John Parker Harrison is distinct from the Wisconsin historian of Britain represented by these students.
